events.title: The 2023–Present Gaza War, Regional Escalation, and International Supply Chains
events.summary: The ongoing conventional military offensive conducted by the Israel Defense Forces ('Operation Swords of Iron') in the Gaza Strip following the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel. The campaign has been characterized by unprecedented levels of aerial bombardment, total naval, land, and aerial blockade, mass forced displacement of over 1.9 million people (85–90% of the population), and widespread destruction of civic, educational, and medical infrastructure. The operation has been directly sustained by emergency diplomatic protection, logistical airlifts, and arms transfers from the United States (tens of thousands of precision bombs, 155mm shells, and bunker busters) and the United Kingdom (F-35 component manufacturing and daily RAF Akrotiri aerial surveillance flights). Crucially, the campaign is powered by an extensive corporate technological architecture: sovereign cloud computing and AI under 'Project Nimbus' (Google Cloud and Amazon Web Services), battlefield AI battle-management software from Palantir Technologies, enterprise cloud systems from Microsoft, and military networking hardware from Cisco and HPE. Whistleblower intelligence reports documented the deployment of automated AI targeting programs—notably 'Lavender' (generating kill lists of tens of thousands of suspected targets with pre-authorized civilian collateral thresholds), 'The Gospel' (generating structural targets at industrial speed), and 'Where's Daddy?' (tracking targets to family homes before striking)—prompting formal genocide proceedings at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and corporate complicity filings at the International Criminal Court (ICC).

events.title: The 1953 Iranian Coup d'État (Operation Ajax / TPAJAX)
events.summary: The covert overthrow of the democratically elected Prime Minister of Iran, Mohammad Mosaddegh, orchestrated by the United States Central Intelligence Agency (Operation TPAJAX) and the British Secret Intelligence Service (Operation Boot). The coup restored absolute monarchical rule under Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi following Mosaddegh's nationalization of Iran's oil industry, which had been monopolized by the British Anglo-Iranian Oil Company.

events.title: The 2003 Invasion of Iraq (Operation Iraqi Freedom)
events.summary: The conventional military invasion and occupation of the Republic of Iraq by a multinational coalition led by the United States and the United Kingdom. The operation overthrew the Ba'athist government of Saddam Hussein based on stated justifications concerning unverified stockpiles of weapons of mass destruction (WMD) and alleged ties to al-Qaeda, neither of which were substantiated by subsequent exhaustive post-invasion searches.

events.title: The Sabra and Shatila Massacre (September 1982)
events.summary: The slaughter of between 700 and 3,500 predominantly Palestinian and Lebanese Shiite civilians in the Sabra and Shatila refugee camps in West Beirut by Lebanese Christian Phalangist (Kataeb) militia forces, conducted while the perimeter was controlled and illuminated by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) under Defense Minister Ariel Sharon following the 1982 Israeli invasion of Lebanon.

companies.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
companies.operational_role: Joint prime contractor alongside Google under the $1.2 billion 'Project Nimbus' framework, providing scalable cloud infrastructure, elastic compute servers, and enterprise data repositories to the Israeli government and defense sector.

companies.name: Anglo-Iranian Oil Company (AIOC)
companies.operational_role: Exclusive concessionaire operating Iran's oil extraction and the Abadan refinery under highly unfavorable royalty agreements for Iran.

companies.name: BAE Systems plc
companies.operational_role: Britain's largest defense contractor; tier-one global partner producing approximately 15% of the value of every F-35 Lightning II aircraft, including the rear fuselage, electronic warfare suite, and fuel systems.

companies.name: The Boeing Company (Boeing Defense, Space & Security)
companies.operational_role: Primary manufacturer of precision-guided strike weapons kits, AH-64 Apache attack helicopters, and F-15 fighter aircraft utilized by the United States Air Force and Israeli Air Force.

companies.name: Cisco Systems, Inc.
companies.operational_role: Primary provider of high-security networking hardware, encrypted switches, routers, and server infrastructure powering the core communication grids of the Israel Defense Forces and Ministry of Defense.

companies.name: Elbit Systems Ltd.
companies.operational_role: Israel's largest domestic defense contractor; manufacturer of over 85% of Israel's unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), tactical intelligence systems, guided mortar munitions (Iron Sting), and land warfare optics.

companies.name: General Dynamics Corporation
companies.operational_role: Primary prime manufacturer of heavy aerial bomb bodies (MK-84 2,000-lb and MK-82 500-lb) and 155mm M107/M795 artillery projectiles for the US military and allied foreign militaries.

companies.name: Google LLC (Alphabet Inc.)
companies.operational_role: Joint prime contractor with Amazon Web Services under 'Project Nimbus', a $1.2 billion contract providing localized sovereign cloud computing, data centers, and advanced artificial intelligence and machine learning platforms to the Israeli government and Ministry of Defense.

companies.name: Halliburton / Kellogg Brown & Root (KBR)
companies.operational_role: Primary prime logistics and infrastructure contractor under the US Army Logistics Civil Augmentation Program (LOGCAP III) during the 2003 invasion and occupation of Iraq.

companies.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) / HP Inc.
companies.headquarters: Spring, Texas / Palo Alto, California, United States
companies.operational_role: Long-term prime enterprise server, storage architecture, and IT infrastructure provider for the Israeli Ministry of Defense, Israel Defense Forces, and the Israel Prison Service (IPS).

companies.name: Lockheed Martin Corporation
companies.operational_role: World's largest defense contractor; primary manufacturer of tactical aircraft, precision-guided missiles, radar systems, and air defense platforms for the US military and foreign military sales allies including Israel.

companies.name: Microsoft Corporation
companies.operational_role: Primary enterprise technology, cloud computing (Microsoft Azure), and defense software supplier to the Israeli Ministry of Defense, Israeli security agencies, and the Israel Defense Forces.

companies.name: Palantir Technologies Inc.
companies.operational_role: Specialized defense intelligence software vendor supplying battle-management systems, intelligence fusion platforms (Gotham, Foundry), and the Palantir Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) for military targeting and operational decision-making.

countries.name: Iran
countries.summary: Geopolitically critical Middle Eastern nation subject to intense foreign intervention over control of its vast petroleum reserves, strategically vital Persian Gulf coastline, and regional sphere of influence.

countries.name: Iraq
countries.summary: Mesopotamian state subjected to catastrophic foreign military interventions, including the 1991 Gulf War, twelve years of comprehensive economic sanctions, and the devastating 2003 US-led invasion and occupation.

countries.name: Israel
countries.summary: State established in 1948 whose military, intelligence, and diplomatic interventions have shaped modern Middle Eastern history, foreign occupations, regional wars, and cross-border operations.

countries.name: Lebanon
countries.summary: East Mediterranean nation heavily destabilized by regional proxy conflicts, repeated Israeli military invasions (notably 1978, 1982, 1993, 1996, 2006), and prolonged foreign occupations.

countries.name: Palestine
countries.summary: Territories comprising the West Bank, East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, as well as the global diaspora of millions of Palestinian refugees displaced during successive regional wars.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.summary: Former imperial power in the Middle East and key NATO ally, collaborating closely with the United States and Israel through sovereign military staging bases, aerial intelligence gathering, and defense component manufacturing.

countries.name: United States
countries.summary: Primary global superpower following World War II, conducting global military interventions, covert regime change operations, intelligence alliances, and economic sanctions across Latin America, Asia, and the Middle East.
